I went to a new restaurant near my apartment last week.
It looked busy but nice, so I decided to try it out.
I sat at a small table near the window.
A waiter came and took my order quickly.
I ordered soup, a sandwich, and a drink.
He wrote it down on his little notepad and walked away toward the kitchen.
I waited for a while, reading messages on my phone.
Ten minutes passed, then fifteen minutes.
I started to feel hungry and a little impatient about the whole thing.
I looked around and noticed other tables getting their food already.
People who arrived after me were already eating their meals.
I wondered if something was wrong with my order.
I tried to stay patient, but it was getting harder.
After twenty minutes, I decided to ask about it.
I waved at a different waiter walking by my table.
I asked her if she could check on my order for me.
She looked confused and went to check with the kitchen.
A few minutes later, she came back and looked embarrassed about something.
She said my order was never sent to the kitchen at all, and she was very sorry about it.
The first waiter had forgotten to give it to the cooks.
She apologized many times and said she would fix it right away.
She also said the meal would be free because of the mistake.
I said thank you and tried not to be too upset about it.
Mistakes happen, and everyone was very kind about the situation.
My food arrived fifteen minutes later, hot and fresh from the kitchen.
The soup was good, and the sandwich was even better than I expected.
I ate slowly this time and didn't rush at all.
The free meal made the long wait feel much better than before, and my hunger was completely gone by the end.
Before I left, the manager came over to my table personally.
He apologized again and gave me a small discount card for next time.
I thanked him warmly and said I would definitely come back, no hard feelings at all.
I did go back a few weeks later, on a quiet weekday evening.
This time, my order arrived quickly, and everything was completely perfect.
Sometimes one small mistake can turn into a better story than a normal, ordinary visit.
I even told a few friends about it, and now they want to try the place too.
